questions.stem: Which warehouse object saves a SELECT statement under a name and always returns current data, without storing any rows of its own?
options: A view
A table
A stored procedure
A common table expression
questions.answer: A view
questions.explanation: A view is a stored query definition, so selecting from it runs the underlying statement against current data. A table stores rows, a stored procedure is executed rather than selected from, and a common table expression exists only for the duration of the statement that declares it.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Create views, functions, and stored procedures

questions.stem: You need a reusable routine that accepts parameters, runs several statements in order, and is invoked with EXEC. Which object is that?
options: A stored procedure
A view
A table-valued parameter
A materialized view
questions.answer: A stored procedure
questions.explanation: Stored procedures hold multiple statements, take parameters, and are invoked with EXEC, which makes them the natural home for a multi-step transformation. A view is a single query with no parameters and cannot contain procedural logic.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Create views, functions, and stored procedures

questions.stem: A warehouse view needs to join one of its own tables to a table that lives in a lakehouse in the same workspace. Is that possible, and how?
options: Yes, by writing a cross-database query using three-part names
No, a view can only reference tables in its own warehouse
Only if the lakehouse table is first copied into the warehouse
Only from a Spark notebook, never from T-SQL
questions.answer: Yes, by writing a cross-database query using three-part names
questions.explanation: Warehouses and lakehouse SQL analytics endpoints in the same workspace can be queried together with three-part naming, so a view can join across them without copying data. That is one of the strongest arguments for keeping a lakehouse and a warehouse side by side rather than duplicating tables.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Create views, functions, and stored procedures

questions.stem: In Power Query, which action adds a column whose values are calculated from other columns in the same row?
options: Add Custom Column
Group By
Merge Queries
Transpose
questions.answer: Add Custom Column
questions.explanation: Add Custom Column takes an M expression and evaluates it once per row, which is how a derived value such as line total or a category flag is produced. Group By aggregates, Merge joins another query, and Transpose swaps rows and columns.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Enrich data by adding new columns or tables

questions.stem: In a lakehouse notebook, which PySpark method returns a DataFrame with an additional derived column?
options: withColumn
select
groupBy
filter
questions.answer: withColumn
questions.explanation: withColumn returns a new DataFrame with the named column added or replaced, which is the usual way to derive a value in Spark. select projects existing columns, groupBy prepares an aggregation, and filter removes rows.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Enrich data by adding new columns or tables

questions.stem: Reports need to slice by fiscal quarter and day of week, but the source system supplies only a transaction date. What is the standard way to enable that?
options: Add a date dimension table covering the required range and relate it to the fact table
Add a calculated column to the fact table for every attribute needed
Ask the source system owner to add the columns
Use a slicer on the raw transaction date
questions.answer: Add a date dimension table covering the required range and relate it to the fact table
questions.explanation: A date dimension is generated rather than sourced, and it carries every calendar attribute a report might need. Putting those attributes on the fact table instead repeats them on every row and gives no place to hold dates with no transactions.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Enrich data by adding new columns or tables

questions.stem: In a star schema, which table holds the numeric measures and the foreign keys pointing at the surrounding tables?
options: The fact table
A dimension table
A bridge table
The date table
questions.answer: The fact table
questions.explanation: The fact table sits at the centre and holds the events being measured, one row per event, with foreign keys out to the dimensions that describe them. Dimensions hold the descriptive attributes used to filter and group.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a lakehouse or warehouse

questions.stem: What is the main analytical advantage of a star schema over one very wide table containing every attribute?
options: Filters applied to small dimension tables propagate to the large fact table, so queries stay simple and fast
It removes the need to define any relationships
It guarantees the data is stored in third normal form
It allows more rows to be loaded per table
questions.answer: Filters applied to small dimension tables propagate to the large fact table, so queries stay simple and fast
questions.explanation: Dimensions are small and highly repetitive, so filtering them is cheap, and the relationship carries that filter to the fact table. A single wide table repeats every attribute on every fact row, which is larger, slower to scan, and harder to maintain when an attribute changes.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a lakehouse or warehouse

questions.stem: Why is a surrogate key usually preferred over the source system's business key as the primary key of a dimension?
options: It stays stable when the source key changes or is reused, and it supports tracking history in the dimension
It is always smaller than the business key
It removes the need for a relationship to the fact table
It prevents duplicate rows from ever being loaded
questions.answer: It stays stable when the source key changes or is reused, and it supports tracking history in the dimension
questions.explanation: Business keys are owned by the source and can be re-issued, reformatted or reused, and a dimension that tracks history needs several rows for the same business entity. A surrogate key is generated by the warehouse, so it can identify each version independently of whatever the source does.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a lakehouse or warehouse

questions.stem: What does it mean to denormalize data for analytics?
options: Combine related tables so that fewer joins are needed at query time
Split a table into smaller tables to remove repetition
Remove all duplicate rows from a table
Convert every column to its narrowest data type
questions.answer: Combine related tables so that fewer joins are needed at query time
questions.explanation: Denormalizing folds attributes from related tables into one, trading storage and some repetition for fewer joins. Splitting tables to remove repetition is normalization, which is the opposite move and the right one for transactional systems.

questions.stem: What is the principal cost of denormalizing?
options: The same attribute is repeated on many rows, so a change has to be applied everywhere it appears
Queries always run more slowly
Relationships can no longer be defined
The data can no longer be stored in Delta format
questions.answer: The same attribute is repeated on many rows, so a change has to be applied everywhere it appears
questions.explanation: Repetition is exactly what denormalization buys performance with. The risk is update anomalies: a category renamed in one place and not another leaves the data inconsistent, which is why analytics pipelines rebuild denormalized tables rather than editing them in place.

questions.stem: A source model has Product related to ProductSubcategory, which is related to ProductCategory. What is the usual step to turn this into a star schema?
options: Flatten subcategory and category attributes into a single Product dimension
Relate ProductCategory directly to the fact table
Leave the chain intact, since it is already normalized
Create a bridge table between Product and ProductCategory
questions.answer: Flatten subcategory and category attributes into a single Product dimension
questions.explanation: That chain is a snowflake. Folding the levels into one Product dimension gives a star, with one hop from fact to dimension and simpler, faster filtering. A bridge table is for many-to-many relationships, which this is not.

questions.stem: A fact table holds one row per transaction. Why might you build an additional table aggregated to one row per product per day?
options: Far fewer rows have to be scanned, so summary queries run much faster
It removes the need for a date dimension
It makes the original transaction rows unnecessary
Aggregated tables cannot be filtered, which simplifies the model
questions.answer: Far fewer rows have to be scanned, so summary queries run much faster
questions.explanation: An aggregate table trades detail for speed: a report that only needs daily totals reads orders of magnitude fewer rows. The detailed table is normally kept as well, because anything needing transaction-level analysis still requires it.

questions.stem: In Power Query, what does the Group By transformation produce?
options: One row per distinct combination of the grouping columns, with the requested aggregations
The original rows, sorted by the grouping columns
A separate query for each group
One row per source row, with a group number added
questions.answer: One row per distinct combination of the grouping columns, with the requested aggregations
questions.explanation: Group By collapses the table to the chosen grain and computes aggregations such as sum, count or max for each group. If the detail is still needed afterwards, it has to be kept in a separate query, because Group By discards it.

questions.stem: Before aggregating a fact table to a monthly grain, what must you establish?
options: The lowest grain any current or planned report needs, since detail below the aggregate is lost
That the fact table has fewer than one million rows
That every dimension has a surrogate key
That the source system supports incremental refresh
questions.answer: The lowest grain any current or planned report needs, since detail below the aggregate is lost
questions.explanation: Grain is a one-way decision: once a table is stored at monthly grain there is no way to answer a daily question from it. Deciding the required grain first is the single most consequential step in designing an aggregate, which is why it is worth writing down before any code is built.

questions.stem: You need every order row kept, with customer details attached where a matching customer exists and blanks where none does. Which join is that?
options: Left outer join
Inner join
Right anti join
Full outer join
questions.answer: Left outer join
questions.explanation: A left outer join keeps all rows from the left table and fills unmatched columns from the right with nulls. An inner join would silently drop orders with no matching customer, which is exactly the kind of quiet data loss that is hard to notice later.

questions.stem: In Power Query, what is the difference between Merge Queries and Append Queries?
options: Merge joins on matching columns and adds columns; Append stacks rows from tables with the same shape
Merge stacks rows; Append joins on matching columns
Merge works only on files; Append works only on databases
They are two names for the same operation
questions.answer: Merge joins on matching columns and adds columns; Append stacks rows from tables with the same shape
questions.explanation: Merge is a join: it widens the table. Append is a union: it lengthens it. Reaching for the wrong one is a common early mistake, and the symptom is either duplicated columns or a table with twice the rows and half the values missing.

questions.stem: After joining two tables on a key that is not unique on either side, the result has far more rows than either input. What happened?
options: Each matching row on the left paired with every matching row on the right, multiplying the rows
The join silently switched to a full outer join
Duplicate rows were added by the engine to preserve row order
The key column was converted to text, breaking the match
questions.answer: Each matching row on the left paired with every matching row on the right, multiplying the rows
questions.explanation: A join produces the cross product of matching rows, so a key appearing three times on the left and four on the right yields twelve rows. Sums computed afterwards are then inflated. The fix is to make the key unique on at least one side, usually by aggregating or de-duplicating first.

questions.stem: In Power Query, which action removes rows that repeat an identical combination of the selected columns?
options: Remove Duplicates
Remove Errors
Remove Blank Rows
Keep Top Rows
questions.answer: Remove Duplicates
questions.explanation: Remove Duplicates keeps the first occurrence of each distinct combination across the columns you have selected, which is why selecting the right columns first matters: run it on the whole table and only fully identical rows go.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify and resolve duplicate data, missing data, or null values

questions.stem: Which T-SQL predicate correctly finds rows where a column holds no value?
options: WHERE ShippedDate IS NULL
WHERE ShippedDate = NULL
WHERE ShippedDate = ''
WHERE ShippedDate <> ShippedDate
questions.answer: WHERE ShippedDate IS NULL
questions.explanation: NULL is the absence of a value rather than a value, so any comparison with = returns unknown and the row is not returned. IS NULL is the only correct test. An empty string is a value and is not the same thing as NULL.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify and resolve duplicate data, missing data, or null values

questions.stem: A column of survey scores contains nulls where a respondent skipped the question. Why is replacing those nulls with 0 risky before computing an average?
options: Averages ignore nulls but include zeros, so the result is dragged down by people who did not answer
Zero cannot be stored in a numeric column that allows nulls
It prevents the column from being used in a relationship
The average function will return an error
questions.answer: Averages ignore nulls but include zeros, so the result is dragged down by people who did not answer
questions.explanation: Aggregations treat null as absent: AVG divides by the count of non-null values. Substituting 0 turns a non-answer into a very low answer and changes both the numerator and the denominator. Replacing nulls is sometimes right, but it is a modelling decision rather than tidying up.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify and resolve duplicate data, missing data, or null values

questions.stem: A key column arrives as text but contains only digits. Why convert it to an integer before loading?
options: It stores and compresses better, sorts numerically, and joins faster
Text columns cannot participate in joins at all
It is required before the column can be made nullable
Text columns are not supported in Delta tables
questions.answer: It stores and compresses better, sorts numerically, and joins faster
questions.explanation: Numeric types are narrower, compress far better in a columnar format, and compare faster than strings. Text keys also sort lexically, so 10 sorts before 9, which produces confusing results in any range filter or ordering.

questions.stem: During a type change in Power Query, some values cannot be converted. What happens to them?
options: They become errors in that column, which you can then keep, remove or replace
They are silently set to null
The whole query fails and no rows are returned
They are left in their original type
questions.answer: They become errors in that column, which you can then keep, remove or replace
questions.explanation: Power Query marks unconvertible values as errors rather than guessing or discarding them, and gives you Remove Errors and Replace Errors to decide what should happen. Treating errors as null by reflex hides the fact that source data did not match the expected shape.

questions.stem: A text column holds dates written as 03/04/2026. What must be specified so the conversion is not ambiguous?
options: The locale to use, since the same text means March 4th or April 3rd depending on it
The time zone of the source system
Whether the column allows nulls
The target column's compression setting
questions.answer: The locale to use, since the same text means March 4th or April 3rd depending on it
questions.explanation: Day-first and month-first conventions produce different dates from identical text, and the failure is silent for any day up to the twelfth. Power Query offers Using Locale on the type change so the interpretation is explicit rather than inherited from whoever happens to run the refresh.

questions.stem: Why is it good practice to filter rows as early as possible in a transformation?
options: Every later step then has less data to process, so the whole query is faster
Filters can only be applied before any other transformation
It guarantees the query will fold to the source
Later filters are ignored by the engine
questions.answer: Every later step then has less data to process, so the whole query is faster
questions.explanation: Work removed early is work no subsequent step has to do, and in a query that folds it can also mean far fewer rows crossing the network. Filtering late is one of the most common causes of a slow refresh.

questions.stem: What does it mean when a Power Query filter step folds?
options: It is translated into the source system's own query language and executed there
It is combined with the next step to save memory
It is cached so later refreshes can skip it
It is applied twice, once locally and once at the source
questions.answer: It is translated into the source system's own query language and executed there
questions.explanation: Query folding pushes the work down to the source, so the database does the filtering and only the surviving rows travel. Once a step cannot be folded, everything after it is processed locally, which is why the order of steps affects performance so much.

questions.stem: A refresh that used to be fast has become slow after a change. Which change is most likely to have stopped the query folding?
options: A custom column using an M function the source cannot express was added before the filters
A filter on a date column was made more restrictive
A column was renamed
The rows were sorted by an indexed column
questions.answer: A custom column using an M function the source cannot express was added before the filters
questions.explanation: Folding continues only while every step can be translated into the source's query language. A custom column using a function with no equivalent breaks that chain, and every step after it, including the filters, then runs locally over the full dataset. Renames and simple filters normally fold without trouble.
